edges.limitations: The vitreous separates from the inner limiting membrane in the mouse, whereas patients show an abnormally adherent interface at surgery; high myopia and retinal detachment are not reported in the mouse.
Mice lack a macula, so the human macular atrophy cannot be modelled directly.
Hydrocephalus is background-dependent (C57BL) and the choroid plexus has not been examined in patients.

nodes.description: Collagen XVIII anchors vitreous collagen fibrils to the inner limiting membrane. In Col18a1-null mice the vitreous separates from the inner limiting membrane; in patients the vitreous is syneretic or optically empty and the vitreoretinal interface is abnormally adherent at surgery. The two observations differ, so the exact human interface defect is not settled.

nodes.description: Collagen XVIII is a heparan sulfate proteoglycan of basement membranes. In the eye it is present in every basement membrane except Descemet's membrane, including the inner limiting membrane, Bruch's membrane and the iris pigment epithelium basement membrane; it is also present in the choroid plexus epithelial basement membrane and the developing cortex. Its absence alters basement membrane structure in each of these sites.
